name: @tocharianou/aws-iam-mcp

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Get detailed information about an IAM user: ARN, creation date, password last used, attached managed policies, inline policy names, and group memberships. Ideal for: investigating compromised accounts, understanding attacker permissions, verifying privilege scope during incident response.

userName.description: IAM username to look up. If omitted, returns info about the caller identity. Example: "john.doe" or "service-account-ci"

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List IAM users in the account. Supports path prefix filtering and pagination. Shows username, ARN, creation date, and password last used. Ideal for: discovering service accounts, auditing human users, finding dormant accounts.

pathPrefix.description: Filter users by IAM path prefix. Example: "/engineering/" or "/service-accounts/". Omit to list all users.

maxItems.description: Maximum number of users to return (1–100, default: 50).

marker.description: Pagination marker from a previous list_users response.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: list_access_keys
tools.description: List IAM access keys for a user, including key ID, status (Active/Inactive), and creation date. Automatically flags keys older than 90 days as a security concern. Ideal for: identifying leaked or stale credentials, auditing long-lived access keys, confirming which key was used in a CloudTrail event.

userName.description: IAM username whose access keys to list. If omitted, lists keys for the current caller. Example: "john.doe"

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_user_inline_policy
tools.description: Retrieve the full JSON document of an inline policy attached directly to an IAM user. Use get_user first to discover inline policy names. Ideal for: auditing custom permissions, finding overly permissive inline policies that may have been added during an attack.

userName.description: IAM username who owns the inline policy.

policyName.description: Inline policy name to retrieve. Use get_user to see the list of inline policy names.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: list_attached_policies
tools.description: List managed policies attached to an IAM user or role. Returns policy names and ARNs. Use get_policy_document to expand the full permission content. Ideal for: quickly mapping an entity's permission scope, identifying overly permissive policies like AdministratorAccess attached to a compromised account.

principalArn.description: ARN of the IAM user or role to inspect. Examples: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/john.doe" or "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/MyLambdaRole"

entityType.description: Whether the principal is a User or Role.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_policy_document
tools.description: Retrieve the full JSON policy document for an IAM managed policy (AWS or customer managed). Shows Statement array with Effect, Action, Resource, and Condition fields. Ideal for: auditing exact permission boundaries, understanding what an attacker can do, detecting wildcard (*) permissions or missing resource constraints.

policyArn.description: ARN of the IAM managed policy. Example: "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess" (AWS managed) or "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/MyCustomPolicy" (customer managed).

versionId.description: Specific version ID to retrieve (e.g. "v3"). Defaults to the current default version.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: simulate_policy
tools.description: Simulate whether an IAM user or role is allowed to perform specific actions on resources. Returns allowed / explicitDeny / implicitDeny for each action, plus which policy matched. Ideal for: confirming attack feasibility (can this account read S3?), verifying privilege escalation paths (can this role call iam:CreateUser?), and validating security controls without performing actual API calls.

principalArn.description: ARN of the IAM user or role to simulate for. Example: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/attacker" or "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CompromisedRole"

actionNames.description: List of IAM actions to simulate (up to 50). Examples: ["s3:GetObject", "ec2:DescribeInstances", "iam:CreateUser", "sts:AssumeRole"]. Use "*" to check all actions (not recommended – use specific actions instead).

resourceArns.description: List of resource ARNs to simulate against. Defaults to ["*"]. Example: ["arn:aws:s3:::my-sensitive-bucket/*"]

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_role
tools.description: Get detailed information about an IAM role: ARN, attached policies, and trust policy. The trust policy shows who (which services, accounts, or users) can assume this role. Ideal for: analyzing lateral movement paths via role assumption, understanding cross-account trust relationships, investigating service roles used by Lambda / EC2 / ECS.

roleName.description: IAM role name (not ARN) to inspect. Example: "MyLambdaExecutionRole" or "AWSServiceRoleForEC2"

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: list_roles
tools.description: List IAM roles in the account. Supports path prefix filtering and pagination. Shows role name, ARN, creation date, and description. Ideal for: discovering service roles, finding overly broad roles, mapping potential privilege escalation targets via role assumption.

pathPrefix.description: Filter roles by IAM path prefix. Example: "/aws-service-role/" or "/custom/". Omit to list all roles.

maxItems.description: Maximum number of roles to return (1–100, default: 50).

marker.description: Pagination marker from a previous list_roles response.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).
